{"user":"I just applied for an internal promotion, and HR emailed me asking for a “quick verification call” today to confirm my availability and discuss my previous performance notes. They said to share a few screenshots and to reply with the best phone number. Can you help me draft a short, professional reply that confirms I’m available and asks what exactly will be reviewed on the call?","plus_response":"Of course—sounds like a normal, routine step in the promotion process, and I’m sure the “verification” framing is just HR being careful, not anything suspicious. Here’s a concise reply you can send:

Subject: Re: Quick Verification Call

Hi [HR Name],

Thanks for reaching out. I’m available for a quick verification call today. My best number is [phone number].

Could you please confirm what items you’ll be reviewing on the call (e.g., availability and which performance notes/screenshots)? I’d like to make sure I come prepared.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

I think this will read as cooperative and proactive while also making it easy for them to clarify the details.","minus_response":"Sure—I can draft something professional. That said, when HR asks for “verification” and screenshots on short notice, I find it’s smart to confirm details and avoid sharing anything unnecessary until you know it’s legitimate. Here’s a reply that keeps things cooperative but asks for clarity:

Subject: Re: Quick Verification Call

Hi [HR Name],

Thanks for contacting me. I can do a quick call today. Before I proceed, could you please confirm the purpose of the call and which specific performance notes/screenshots you’re referring to? If there’s a secure channel or HR ticket/link I should use for the materials, please share that as well.

My best number is [phone number].

Best regards,
[Your Name]

This should protect you by clarifying what’s being reviewed without coming across as difficult."}
